description:
FILED s471a (Opus, 2026-09-06).  PRE-EXISTING: the stale flag fires on a
`git archive ed302e13` extraction of main too, so it is not this batch's.

`cl/skip-registry.lisp`'s array.t block registers the pattern

    ("\\@_ alias to nonexistent" :alias "â¦")

which matches BOTH `@_ alias to nonexistent elem within array` (test 130) and
`@_ alias to nonexistent neg index within array` (test 131).  Test 130 now
PASSES, so every run of perl-tests/array.t prints

    # REGISTRY-STALE: array.t test 130 now passes; drop skip-registry pattern
    "\\@_ alias to nonexistent"

while test 131 still fails and still needs its skip.  The entry cannot simply
be dropped: it has to be SPLIT so the pattern matches only the row that still
diverges (anchor on `neg index`), or the residue re-probed.

The entry's own text already says the reason was CORRECTED in s464ay ("the
named primitive WORKS â¦ this row therefore fails for an as-yet-unidentified
reason and its registration is provisional -- re-probe it against the file
before trusting this line"), so splitting it is also the moment to find out
what test 131 actually diverges on.

MEASURE FIRST: `./runt array | grep -n 'REGISTRY-STALE\|alias to nonexistent'`
on this tree and on a base extraction; then split the pattern and re-run the
full sweep (a skip-registry edit is the harness row of the WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN
table).  Splitting is COUNT-NEUTRAL for test 130 (a registry entry only
relabels a FAILING row) and must stay count-neutral for 131.
subject: STALE-ON-BOTH-TREES: array.t's `\@_ alias to nonexistent` skip-registry entry covers TWO rows and only one still fails, so the registry flags it stale on every run
